battle.name: 真州之戰
battle.theater: 長江下游真州與兩淮前線
battle.brief: 1236年，金朝右丞相移剌蒲阿與劉和尚自蔡州敗退至真州，據長江北岸的兩淮重鎮死守。蒙古軍以配重投石車等攻城器械連日轟擊城牆與城樓，同時掘地道、施毒煙破壞牆基，城終於陷落。金將戰死，金朝殘餘勢力自河南至淮右一併清除，南宋輸糧助金的門戶之策也在此役中付出代價。

kit.name: 配重投石車
kit.history: 長臂配重把石頭甩過城牆。工程比攻城武器更早決定勝負。

countries: 交戰的兩方是蒙古軍與金朝殘軍，南宋則是同時被捲入的第三方。金方在蔡州陷落之後已失去中央，留在河南與淮右的兵權集中在右丞相移剌蒲阿手中；此人是契丹出身，早年仕遼，後歸金朝，官至樞密副使、右丞相，與昭勇大將軍劉和尚同為金哀宗倚重的兩名主將。移剌蒲阿在蔡州收拾殘卒，收攏河南、淮右四散的契丹、女真、漢人將校，合軍退保真州，兵員約數萬而精銳有限；這支部隊的糧秣仰賴南宋供給，指揮系統是崩解之後臨時拼湊的，樞密院的舊制只剩名號。蒙古方是窝闊台的帝國，1234年大汗死後乃馬真臨朝聽政，拔都又率精銳西征，留在南面的兵力由諸王與萬戶分統；負責江淮方向的一支以河南、山東為基地，圍城時把兵分為砲隊、穴地隊、步卒圍城隊與騎兵封鎖隊，攻城與野戰同時進行。南宋則處在最尷尬的位置：端平年間宋廷曾出糧借蒙古之力滅金，1234年趙葵的端平入洛失敗之後蒙古轉而南向，宋廷一面加固兩淮城防、囤積糧草，一面仍舊接濟真州的金軍以牽制蒙古，輸糧的船隊與運兵的道路走的是同一條江。正因如此，真州一城同時被三方爭奪，它的存亡直接牽動淮右的整條防線。
countriesEn: The two belligerents were the Mongol army and the rump Jin army, while the Southern Song was a third party dragged into the same theatre. On the Jin side the central government had already vanished with the fall of Caizhou, and what authority remained in Henan and the lands north of the Huai was concentrated in the hands of the Right Chancellor Yelü Pu'a. He was of Khitan origin, had served the Liao court in his youth, came over to the Jin, and rose to be Deputy Director of the Privy Council and Right Chancellor; together with the General of Martial Valour Liu Heshang he was one of the two commanders on whom Jin Aizong relied. After Caizhou fell, Yelü Pu'a gathered up the broken troops, collected the Khitan, Jurchen and Chinese officers scattered over Henan and the Huai country, and withdrew to guard Zhenzhou with a force of some tens of thousands of men but few trained soldiers; that force was kept alive on grain supplied by the Southern Song, and its command structure was no more than a hastily patched survival of a broken system, the old institutions of the Privy Council surviving as titles rather than as functions. The Mongol side was the empire of Ogedei; after the Great Khan died in 1234 his widow Ogedei took the regency while Batu led a picked force west, so that the troops remaining in the south were commanded by the princes and the myriad commands in separate bodies. The column responsible for the Jianghuai direction operated from bases in Henan and Shandong, and when it invested a city it divided its men into artillery sections, sappers, infantry forming the cordon, and cavalry charged with sealing the approaches, so that siege and field operations went forward at the same time. The Southern Song stood in the most awkward position of the three: during the Duanping years the court had sent grain to the Mongols to help them destroy the Jin, and after Zhao Kui's Duanping advance on Luoyang had failed the Mongols turned south, so the Song both fortified the cities of the Two Huai and stored grain, and at the same time continued to feed the Jin army at Zhenzhou in order to pin the Mongols down; the grain boats and the marching columns used the same river. For that reason Zhenzhou was contested by all three parties at once, and the fate of the city bore directly on the whole line of the Huai.
people: 核心人物是金方的移剌蒲阿與劉和尚。移剌蒲阿以契丹人仕金，在蒙古南下之前的數十年裡先後當過西面與北面的統帥，是金國倚以支柱北方的人物；金哀宗南奔時把他與劉和尚一併帶到蔡州，城下議和不成、城破在即，他受命收拾殘局，退保真州之後，這支部隊便成了金朝最後的旗籍。劉和尚是金朝宿將，昭勇大將軍，與移剌蒲阿同守蔡州、同奔真州，兩人在真州的最後數月裡分掌城防與江面巡邏，蒙古使者來招降時沒有屈從，最終死於城破之役，具體情形有被亂軍所殺、自裁與投江諸說。金哀宗完顏守緒在汴京失守之後退蔡州，1234年正月遣使議和被蒙古扣留，二月城破之前自縊於幽蘭軒，把帝位傳給宗室完顏承麟，承麟在城陷當日的戰鬥中身亡，完顏氏的皇統就此中斷。蒙古方面的關鍵人物是拔都，他自1235年率軍西征，抽走了最有經驗的一批騎兵，1236年乃馬真臨朝之後的權力競逐又牽制了前線指揮；經略河南的察罕在丙子年前後病故，使蒙古在江淮的攻勢再度中斷。南宋方面，趙葵在端平入洛之後仍奉命主持北伐，兩淮制置使趙善湘整飭沿江城防，孟珙則在荊襄一線收復襄樊等失地，說明宋廷已把主要精力轉向固守長江。
peopleEn: The central figures are Yelü Pu'a and Liu Heshang of the Jin side. Yelü Pu'a was a Khitan who had served the Jin, and in the decades before the Mongols came south he had commanded in the west and in the north, so that he was one of the men on whom the Jin state relied to hold the northern line. When Jin Aizong fled south he brought Yelü Pu'a and Liu Heshang with him to Caizhou; after the failed parley and with the city about to fall, Yelü Pu'a was charged with picking up the pieces, and after falling back on Zhenzhou that remnant force became the last banner of the Jin. Liu Heshang was a long-serving general of the Jin, General of Martial Valour, who had held Caizhou with Yelü Pu'a and broken out with him to Zhenzhou; in the last months of the city's defence the two of them divided the walls and the river watch between them, and when the Mongol envoys came to call for surrender they did not yield, both dying in the storming of the city, the exact manner of their deaths being given variously as cut down in the melee, taken their own lives, or drowned. Jin Aizong, Wanyan Shouxu, had retreated to Caizhou after Bianjing was lost, was held as a hostage when he sent envoys to parley in the first month of 1234, and in the second month, with the city about to fall, hanged himself in Youlan Hall and handed the throne to the clan prince Wanyan Chenglin, who was killed in the fighting on the very day the city fell, so that the imperial line of the Wanyan clan was cut off there. On the Mongol side the key figure was Batu, who led his army west from 1235 and drew away the most experienced cavalry, while the struggle over authority that followed the regency of Ogedei tied down the commanders in the field; Chaghan, the administrator of Henan, died of illness around the bingzi year, and the Mongol offensive in the Jianghuai stalled again. On the Song side Zhao Kui still held command of the northern expedition after the failure at Luoyang, the Two Huai administrator Zhao Shanxiang put the river defences in order, and Meng Gong recovered Xiangyang and other lost ground in the Jingxiang line, all of which shows that the Song court had turned its main effort to holding the river.
kits: 這場戰爭的攻城器械核心是配重投石車。唐宋的攻城砲車一路發展，至十二世紀《武經總要》所載已是成熟的長臂配重形態，以絞盤拉臂、配重加速；十三世紀蒙古入中原之後，此類配重投射器在中土攻城之中更見廣泛使用，《金史》記蔡州之圍已有填充毒煙與火藥的投射器；同一技術經中亞、西亞西傳，歐洲自十一世紀末起稱為trebuchet，義大利諸城邦用它攻破城堡，卡面所標一一〇〇年正是這一歐洲早期年代。蒙古軍作戰時配備的攻城砲，以石彈、陶彈為主，專打城樓、角樓與牆頭守軍密集之處；真州是州級城池，牆身兼作水門與江防，砲火的作用不是把整段城牆砸垮，而是壓制城頭射界、削去城樓，令守軍無法在缺口處集結。金人在蔡州之圍已用過填充毒煙與火藥的投射器，《金史》記有毒煙破敵的記載，同類的燃燒性投射器在真州之役中極可能再度出現，但史籍未留下器械名稱。除砲之外，蒙古軍備有撞竿、雲梯、攻城塔、木柵與填壕用的土袋，真正的破城主力則是穴地：先在牆根掘地道，以木柱支撐，柱上燃燒使土牆崩塌，再由突擊隊攀緣而入，攻城塔與雲梯多在缺口打開之後才湧上城頭。守城的宋軍與金軍配備神臂弓、霹靂箭與突火槍一類火器，牆頭備滾木礌石，重要城門還加設木構拒馬。運輸上，蒙古以牛馬馱運數百斤的石彈與木料，並利用真州臨近長江的水路把砲石運到城下；金軍的糧道則完全倚賴南宋由江南運來的船貨，這條補給線一旦被切斷，城內撐不了多久。
kitsEn: The siege engine at the centre of this war was the counterweight trebuchet. The siege throwing engines of Tang and Song China developed in a line until the Wujing Zongyao of the twelfth century already showed the mature long-armed counterweight form, worked by a winch and accelerated by the counterweight; after the Mongols came into China proper in the thirteenth century this class of counterweight projectile was put to more general use in sieges on Chinese soil, and the Jin history records that at the siege of Caizhou there was already a projectile filled with poison smoke and gunpowder; the same technology passed west through Central and Western Asia, and in Europe from the end of the eleventh century it was called the trebuchet, the Italian city-states using it to breach castles, the 1100 on the card being that early European date. The siege artillery carried by the Mongol army used stone and ceramic shot chiefly, and was aimed at the towers and corner bastions of the wall and at the places where the defenders massed on the parapet. Zhenzhou was a prefectural city whose wall also served as a water gate and a river defence, and the function of the artillery was not to smash a whole section of wall down but to dominate the firing positions on top, to destroy the towers, and to prevent the defenders from massing at a breach. The Jin had already used a projectile filled with poison smoke and gunpowder in the siege of Caizhou, the Jin history recording poison smoke used against the attackers, and a similar incendiary projectile was very probably brought into the storming of Zhenzhou, though no name for the machine survives in the sources. Besides the artillery the Mongols brought up battering poles, ladders, siege towers, wooden fences and sacks of earth for filling the ditch, while the real weight of the assault fell on sapping: they dug a gallery under the wall, propped it with timber, burned the props so that the earth wall fell in, and then stormed the breach, the towers and the ladders going up only after the hole had been opened. The Song troops and the Jin remnant had powerful crossbows, thunder-crash fire arrows and fire lances among their equipment, with rolling logs and stones on the parapet and wooden barriers added at the more important gates. On the transport side the Mongols had oxen and horses carrying stones of several hundred jin and heavy timber, and used the water of the Yangtze that ran past Zhenzhou to bring shot up to the walls; the grain road of the Jin, by contrast, depended entirely on cargo boats bringing food up from Jiangnan, and once that line was cut the city could not hold for long.
tactics: 蒙古的攻城套路在十三世紀已經定型：先以遠程砲火消耗城頭的守軍與器械，再以穴地與撞擊把牆身弄鬆，最後集中兵力在一處缺口突入，並在突圍之前對外圍援軍反覆出擊，切斷援兵與糧道。真州之役裡這套程序大體走得完整，只是因守城一方兵力單薄、援軍無望，最後的決戰變得格外慘烈。移剌蒲阿的部署以守城待援為主軸：他把殘軍分作城防、巡江與突擊三部分，巡江的兵以舟船監視江面，阻止蒙古的船隊在夜裡靠岸，突擊隊則在蒙古遠程砲擊的間隙出城反擊，試圖打亂圍城的節奏。金方也用配重投石車反擊蒙古的砲隊與集兵地，但以當時的配重投石車而言，射程與射速都受繩索與配重所限，只能打近處的目標，難以壓制蒙古在城外寬闊地帶上展開的攻城器械與騎兵。決定真州命運的其實是三件事：一是穴地與內部的崩潰，二是糧道，蒙古封鎖楚州、泗州一線的水陸路，南宋的運糧船隊無法再北上；三是蒙古內部的牽制，拔都西征、乃馬真臨朝與察罕病故使前線無法長期維持高強度，攻城得手之後便轉為收兵北撤，城下得解的那部分金軍因此沒有被全數殲滅，但主力仍被封在城中。
tacticsEn: The Mongol method of investing a city had settled into a fixed form by the thirteenth century: first long-range artillery fire wore down the defenders and their machines on the parapet, then sapping and battering loosened the body of the wall, and finally the troops were concentrated on a single breach, with repeated sorties against relief armies to cut off both reinforcements and supply. In the siege of Zhenzhou that procedure was broadly followed, but because the defenders were few and no relief was coming, the last assault was unusually hard. Yelü Pu'a organised the defence on the assumption of holding the city until help came: he divided the remnant force into the wall garrison, the river watch and the strike teams; the river watch used boats to keep watch on the water and stop Mongol craft coming ashore at night, and the strike teams went out through the gates during the lulls in the artillery bombardment to try to break the rhythm of the investment. The Jin also used their own counterweight trebuchets to fire back at the Mongol artillery parks and assembly points, but a trebuchet of the period, limited in range and rate of fire by its ropes and its counterweight, could only strike at close targets and had little effect on the siege engines and cavalry deployed across the wide ground outside the walls. What really decided Zhenzhou was three things: the sapping and the internal collapse of the wall; the grain road, with the Mongols closing the water and land routes around Chuizhou and Suzhou so that the Song grain boats could no longer go north; and the restraints inside the Mongol camp, since Batu's western expedition, the regency of Ogedei and the death of Chaghan meant the front could not be held at high intensity for long, and after the city fell the Mongols withdrew north. Part of the Jin force inside the city was therefore not destroyed, though the main body was shut in and overwhelmed.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。蒙古滅金的戰爭自1211年野狐嶺起，至1236年真州之戰收尾，前後二十五年；1214年蒙古軍攻中都，1215年起分三路掃平河北，1231至1232年三路大軍合攻，金國主力覆滅，1233年又失開封，蔡州最後的抵抗便只剩下遷都的亡國之師。1233年冬蒙古軍抵達蔡州，圍城約三個月，1234年二月蔡州城破，金哀宗自縊，完顏承麟同日戰死。移剌蒲阿所部自蔡州退保真州，行程自今河南汝南經商丘、徐州、楚州而至江蘇鎮江，迂迴逾一千五百里，橫跨兩個冬天。關於真州金軍的兵數，各家記載多作數萬之眾，較為可靠的說法是收攏了蔡州潰卒與河南、淮右散兵，其中可戰之卒僅數千；城陷之時突圍與死守者，數千人被殲或被俘。蒙古方面的總動員，編年史家多作數十萬之估計，但同時壓到江淮前線的實際部隊當以萬計。蒙古軍自1236年起對宋的攻勢涵蓋京西、荊湖與兩淮三路，1237年起部分兵馬自兩淮與荊湖收縮北還，江淮戰線因此相對沉寂數年；孟珙趁勢收復襄樊，1239年蒙古再攻壽州、廬州一線仍然無功。蒙古真正把兵鋒壓到宋境核心，是1259年攻鄂州與1267至1273年的襄樊、釣魚城之役，前後又用了二十六年，直到1276年臨安出降、1279年崖山失守。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. The Mongol war against the Jin lasted twenty-five years, from the fight at Yehuling in 1211 to the end of the business at Zhenzhou in 1236: the Mongols took Zhongdu in 1214, swept the northern plain in three columns from 1215, and in 1231 and 1232 the three Mongol armies closed in and the main strength of the Jin was destroyed, followed by the loss of Bianjing in 1233. The Mongol army reached Caizhou in the winter of 1233 and held the city for about three months; in the second month of 1234 Caizhou fell, Jin Aizong hanged himself and Wanyan Chenglin was killed the same day. The force under Yelü Pu'a marched from Caizhou to Zhenzhou by way of today's Runan in Henan, Shangqiu, Xuzhou and Chuzhou to Zhenjiang in Jiangsu, a detour of more than fifteen hundred li, spread across two winters. As to the number of Jin troops at Zhenzhou, the accounts mostly speak of tens of thousands, the more reliable statement being that the men were collected from the Caizhou strays and from the scattered soldiers of Henan and the Huai country, with only some thousands fit for battle; when the city fell, the thousands who tried to break out were killed or captured. The overall Mongol mobilisation is estimated by the chroniclers in tens of thousands, but the troops actually pushed to the Jianghuai front at one time must be counted in the tens of thousands. The Mongol offensive against the Song from 1236 covered three lines, the capital region, Jinghu and the Two Huai, and from 1237 part of the army was drawn back from the Two Huai and Jinghu, so that the Jianghuai front lay relatively quiet for several years; Meng Gong used the time to recover Xiangyang, and a renewed Mongol attack on the Shouzhou and Luzhou line in 1239 came to nothing. It was not until 1259, with the attack on Ezhou, and the sieges of Xiangfan and Diaoyucheng between 1267 and 1273, that the Mongol blade was driven deep into the heart of Song territory, and even then it took another twenty-six years, until Lin'an surrendered in 1276 and Yashan was lost in 1279.
cause: 真州之戰是金朝崩解的最後一段，而不是一場孤立的攻城。金朝走到這一步有它自己的路徑：海陵王南征失敗、宣宗南渡與中都淪陷，已把北方的根據地與宗室、府庫一併丟掉；1231至1232年三路大軍破金主力於富平、汴京，1233年又失開封，蔡州最後的抵抗便只剩下遷都的亡國之師。蒙古方面的轉向同樣明確：1234年窝闊台死，1235年拔都西征抽走大軍，蒙古本無暇南顧，但金朝既亡，南宋的邊界就直接暴露在河南與山東的蒙古軍面前。真州之所以成為焦點，是因為它在地理上正卡在蒙古的南下通道與南宋的漕運線之間，蒙古必須拿下它才能把河南、山東與江淮連成一條完整的攻勢線，金朝則靠它保住最後的旗籍與南宋的接濟。直接導火線是移剌蒲阿的拒降與整編：蒙古在蔡州之後曾屢次遣使勸降，移剌蒲阿不從，反而四出招集散兵、在淮右重建了一個可以作戰的集團，這在蒙古看來是不能容許的威脅；對南宋而言，同樣的招集又意味著自己一方面餵養了一支日後可能反噬的軍隊，另一方面卻坐視蒙古的砲火逼近自家城寨。政策上的自相矛盾，把真州推成了三方必爭之地。
causeEn: The battle of Zhenzhou was the last stage of the break-up of the Jin and not an isolated siege. The Jin had walked into it by its own road: the defeat of the Prince of Hailing in the south, the flight of the river by Xuanzong, and the loss of Zhongdu had already stripped the state of its northern base, the clan and the treasuries together; the three Mongol armies destroyed the main Jin strength at Fuping and Bianjing in 1231 and 1232, Bianjing was lost in 1233, and the last resistance at Caizhou was all that remained of a state in flight. The Mongol turn was equally clear: with Ogedei dead in 1234 and Batu's western expedition drawing away the great army from 1235, the Mongols had no attention to spare for the south; but once the Jin was gone the Song border lay exposed to the Mongol armies in Henan and Shandong. Zhenzhou became the focus because it stood geographically across the road by which the Mongols came south and the waterway by which the Song fed itself, and the Mongols had to take it to string Henan, Shandong and the Jianghuai into one continuous line of advance, while the Jin needed it to keep the last of its banner and its connection with Song grain. The immediate occasion was Yelü Pu'a's refusal to surrender and his work of reorganisation: after Caizhou the Mongols sent envoys to call for submission more than once, and Yelü Pu'a refused, going further out to gather scattered soldiers and to rebuild a fighting force on the Huai, which the Mongols could not tolerate as a threat. For the Song the same gathering was equally unwelcome, since it meant feeding a force that might one day turn on its own donors, while sitting still under the Mongol guns opposite its own cities. The contradiction in policy is what pushed Zhenzhou into the position of a place that all three parties had to fight for.
impact: 這場戰役的結果被後世史家當作金朝真正滅亡的年份：金政權的中央在1234年已斷，旗籍與軍力卻在淮右又撐了兩年，到真州陷落才被徹底清掉，中原與淮右自此完全歸入蒙古的版圖，漢人建立的北方王朝自此不再復辟。對南宋而言，這是一段難得的教訓，出糧借外力滅金雖換來了兩年喘息，卻也坐實了與蒙古共處一線的格局，端平入洛的敗績更讓朝野明白借來的刀終究指向自己，之後二十年的國策便從收復中原轉為倚江自守。技術上的收穫更為實際：蔡州與真州兩役把蒙古的攻城工程系統化，砲火壓制、穴地破牆、燃燒器械與迫降手段被整合成一套可以反覆套用的辦法，這套經驗在1259年的鄂州、1267至1273年的襄樊與釣魚城再次出場，成為宋元戰爭中每一場硬仗的標準動作。戰略上的影響是江淮戰線被拉長：真州陷落之後，宋蒙為這一帶反覆拉鋸，蒙古的內部則因大汗繼位與西征而暫時收兵，江北與淮南都沒有立刻變成蒙古的穩定後方，雙方都獲得了一段重新佈局的時間，而這段時間最終被蒙古用來整備火器、籌措海運，並最終完成對南宋的合圍。金源舊事與文物在戰亂與俘獲之中大部散失，契丹、女真貴族則多降為蒙古的附庸，歷代史書對金亡的敘述，也就此被改寫成一部蒙古興起史的尾聲。
impactEn: The result of this battle is taken by later historians as the year in which the Jin truly ended: the central government of the Jin had already been broken in 1234, but the banner and the armed force held on in the lands north of the Huai for two more years, and only with the fall of Zhenzhou were they cleared away, so that Henan and the Huai country passed entirely into the Mongol orbit and no Han-ruled northern state was ever restored. For the Southern Song the lesson was hard: sending grain to a foreign power to destroy the Jin had bought two years of respite, but it also settled the fact that the Song and the Mongols now shared a single line, and the failure of the Duanping advance on Luoyang taught the court at home that a borrowed knife eventually points at the hand that holds it, so that the policy of the next twenty years turned from recovering the north to holding the river. The technical harvest was more practical still: the sieges of Caizhou and Zhenzhou systematised Mongol siege engineering, with artillery suppression, sapping against the wall, incendiary machines and the forced surrender combined into a set of methods that could be applied again and again, and that same expertise appeared at Ezhou in 1259 and at Xiangfan and Diaoyucheng between 1267 and 1273, becoming the standard form of every hard-fought siege in the Song-Yuan wars. Strategically the war was drawn out along the river: after Zhenzhou fell, the Song and the Mongols fought for that district again and again, while on the Mongol side the succession and the western expedition brought a temporary withdrawal, and neither north of the river nor south of the Huai became a settled Mongol rear at once; both sides were given time to re-lay their plans, and the Mongols used that time to perfect their guns, to organise their sea transport and finally to close the ring around the Song. Much of the Jin heritage and its records was lost in the fighting and in the taking of prisoners, while Khitan and Jurchen nobles survived mostly as Mongol vassals, and the way the later histories told the story of the end of the Jin was rewritten as the closing chapter of a history of the Mongol rise.
result: 真州城破，金朝的最後旗籍覆滅。移剌蒲阿與劉和尚死於城破之役，突圍者被殲，降卒被編入蒙古軍隊，餘眾散為流寇或在江淮之間被清剿，金人經營了百年的政權至此連軍隊都不剩。蒙古軍佔領真州，切斷了南宋輸往北方的最後一條接濟線，也把河南、山東與江淮的攻勢連成一體；同年蒙古大舉南下的其他各路同時推進，江北、荊湖與兩淮一齊告急。南宋被迫收縮，把有限的兵力集中到長江防線與荊襄、兩淮幾個要點，趙善湘整理城防、孟珙經營襄樊，數年之間竟靠著蒙古內部的收兵維持住一段安寧。從兵器角度看，這場戰爭給出的答案是含混的：配重投石車這類能越過城牆的器械確實在城頭製造了缺口，卻沒有決定真州的存亡，真正破城的是穴地與內部的崩潰，真正困死守軍的是糧道被切斷。同一個道理在此後的中西戰場上又得到印證，蒙古在歐洲攻破城堡靠的是攻城砲與坑道配合，而不是單靠投石車的射程；蒙古在南方攻宋靠的是水軍、海運與長期圍困，也不是靠砲火一擊而就。終局則在四十三年之後，一二七六年臨安出降，一二七九年崖山失守，宋亡，金的舊疆與南宋的江山一併進入蒙古帝國的版圖，而真州這座因一場攻城而改換旗幟的沿江城鎮，成了這段大變局的起點與縮影。
resultEn: Zhenzhou fell and the last banner of the Jin was destroyed. Yelü Pu'a and Liu Heshang died in the storming, those who broke out were killed, the surrendered were enrolled in the Mongol army, and the remainder scattered as armed bands or were hunted down through the Huai country, so that not a single unit of the army of a state that had lasted a hundred years was left standing. The Mongols occupied Zhenzhou, cut the last line by which the Song had fed the north, and joined Henan, Shandong and the Jianghuai into one line of advance; in the same year the other Mongol columns advanced at the same time, and the north of the river, Jinghu and the Two Huai all became critical at once. The Song was forced to contract, concentrating what little it had on the river line and on the key points of Jingxiang and the Two Huai, with Zhao Shanxiang putting the defences in order and Meng Gong managing Xiangfan, and for several years a kind of peace was kept by the Mongol withdrawal. As to the weapons, the answer this war gives is ambiguous: machines like the counterweight trebuchet, which could throw a stone over a wall, did indeed open gaps on the parapet, but they did not decide the fate of Zhenzhou; what actually broke the wall was sapping and the collapse within, and what actually starved the defenders was the cutting of the grain road. The same lesson was confirmed later on battlefields both east and west: the Mongols took castles in Europe by combining artillery with sapping rather than by the reach of a trebuchet alone, and they took the southern Song by water power, sea transport and long encirclement rather than by a single stroke of artillery. The end came forty-three years later: Lin'an surrendered in 1276, Yashan was lost in 1279, and the Song was gone, the old lands of the Jin and the territories of the Southern Song passing together into the empire of the Mongols, while Zhenzhou, the river city that changed its banners over a single siege, stands as both the beginning and the miniature of that great upheaval.
